newsitem.title: PERU: Peru and Panama unite in war on drug-trafficking.
newsitem.headline: Peru and Panama unite in war on drug-trafficking.

text.p: The leaders of Peru and Panama, both focal points for Latin America's illegal drug trade, agreed on Wednesday to activate a joint anti-trafficking policy body in the first half of 1997.

The drugs' cooperation committee was the most important element in five bilateral accords and a joint declaration signed by Peru's President Alberto Fujimori and Panama's President Ernesto Perez Balladares in Lima's Government Palace.
The declaration promised both nations would unite efforts in "the fight on drug-abuse, narcotics trafficking, money-laundering and related crimes."
Peru is the world's largest producer of coca leaf, the raw product for cocaine, while Panama is considered one of the region's major money-laundering centres.
Panamanian Foreign Minister Ricardo Arias told reporters the committee would help determine the countries' anti-drug policies, but not conduct operations.

Perez Balladares, who arrived in Peru late on Tuesday for a two-day official visit to Peru, added that he had received Fujimori's support for his initiative to create a multinational anti-narcotics centre on an old U.S. military base in Panama.
"Insofar as we can unite our efforts and resources, which are scarce ... we can be more efficient and win this fight," he said.
Balladares was due to meet local businessmen and receive Peru's highest honour, The Order of the Sun, later on Wednesday.
